title: Outside the 30-day window, but an incident is open
question: The window has closed, yet you refund. What changes the answer for this customer?
warning: The 30-day window has closed. Refund only if an open incident hit this customer, otherwise ask your lead.
why: An open incident affects this customer's region. When our outage hit them, the 30-day window does not apply and the refund is on us. (Example policy: window 30 days.)

title: Chargeback already filed: do not refund
question: A chargeback is already filed and you are not refunding. What goes wrong if you do?
warning: Stop. A chargeback is already filed. Refunding now pays the customer twice. Leave a note and let the dispute run.
why: A chargeback is already filed. If I refund as well, the customer is paid twice and we lose the money twice. I leave a note and let the dispute run.

title: Enterprise account: loop in the account manager
question: You escalate instead of refunding. Why does this customer go to someone else?
warning: Enterprise account. Loop in the account manager before any refund or exception. Use Escalate, not Refund.
why: Enterprise accounts have an account manager who owns the relationship and the contract terms. I loop them in before any refund or exception.

title: A threatened public review is not a reason
question: The customer threatens a public review. Does that change your decision?
warning: A threatened public review is not a reason to refund by itself. Decide by policy and facts, not by pressure.
why: A threatened review is not a reason by itself. We decide on policy and facts. Pressure alone never earns a refund or an exception.

title: Never refund to a different card or account
question: The customer wants the money on a different card. What is the rule here?
warning: Never refund to a different card or account than the original payment. It goes back to the original method, even if the card expired.
why: Refunds go back to the original payment method only. A refund to a different card or account is a common fraud pattern.

title: Over the agent limit: second approver
question: This refund is over your limit. Who has to approve it, and why?
warning: Over the example agent refund limit of 250 EUR. Do not press Refund. Escalate for a second approver.
why: Example policy: an agent refunds up to 250 EUR alone. Above that a second approver signs off, so one person never moves a large sum alone.
